key_insight: PU-DDFEM builds reusable local reduced bases and combines them through a partition of unity to approximate strongly anisotropic diffusion in magnetized plasmas.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets lower online simulation costs for plasma transport problems where thin boundary layers make standard finite element mesh refinement expensive.
method: Generate local snapshots by parametrizing magnetic fields and boundary conditions.
Extract dominant local modes through a spectral problem.
Assemble a conforming global approximation using partition-of-unity functions with offline–online separation.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes the construction and intended basis reuse across global magnetic configurations but reports no numerical errors, speedups, or benchmark results.
watch_item: Accuracy for new magnetic configurations may depend on how well the local training parameters cover the relevant field and boundary-condition regimes.
paper_title: Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
